title: Conjunctival and chorioretinal vascular alterations in Osler’s disease
summary:
Osler’s disease (also called hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, HHT) is a rare inherited disorder of the blood vessels. Typical features include abnormal small blood vessels (telangiectasias), which can lead to frequent nosebleeds, organ involvement, and other complications.

This study aims to investigate whether and how the eyes are affected in Osler’s disease. Using modern imaging techniques—such as optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT angiography, and fluorescein angiography—we will examine the blood vessels in the conjunctiva, iris, and retina. In addition, an ear, nose, and throat (ENT) examination will document vascular changes in the nasal and throat areas.

The goal is to systematically describe the frequency and severity of ocular changes and to explore whether these changes are linked to other signs of the disease, such as vascular involvement in internal organs. In the future, eye findings could potentially serve as a “window” to help monitor disease progression and organ involvement in Osler’s disease.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of Osler’s disease according to the Curaçao criteria
- Written informed consent from the patient
- Presentation at the ENT clinic or via contact with the HHT patient support group
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of consent or individuals unable to provide consent
- Pregnancy
- No performance of FLA/ICG in cases of: allergy to contrast agents (e.g., fluorescein/ICG), severely impaired renal function, significantly reduced cardiac function
